rule: The twenty-two standing dissents adjudicated `open_debt` in docs/receipts/standing-dissent-adjudications.json name what is owed but nothing that could be handed to anybody. This is that hand-off. The R-15/R-18 amendment of 2026-08-14 clears a dissent one of exactly two ways -- clause 1, a fresh whole-series re-adjudication, or clause 2, a ruled src/ correction when that re-adjudication sustains the dissent -- and clause 3 forbids a re-run whose superseding receipt names no specific defect in the brief it replaces. Naming that defect concretely, and measuring it from committed artifacts, is the one part of clearing a dissent an implementation lane may do: it is a statement about the QUESTION, never about the answer. Every cluster below carries the defect its members' briefs shared and the measurement that establishes it, and every cluster a fresh investigation can clear additionally carries the well-posed brief clause 1 needs -- so a re-adjudication is a task somebody can start rather than a sentence somebody agrees with. One cluster carries no brief on purpose, because its prior brief has no defect to name and an investigation is the wrong instrument for it; that one is routed to a ruling and says so.
what_this_file_does_not_do: It decides no dissent, and no cluster below states or implies a verdict. Naming a defect in a brief is not answering the question the brief posed: the remedy of every cluster an investigation can clear is still a fresh investigator that has read neither the prior receipts nor this docket, and clause 2 still re-opens the producing correction as a ruled src/ slice if that investigator again certifies the old value. What the docket removes is the state the sign-off review found -- twenty-two debts naming a remedy nobody could begin.
why_a_lane_may_write_this_and_not_the_ve: R-18's export keeps src/, the plan, the diff and the post-change baseline out of an investigator's hands so that its arithmetic is independent. Every fact in this file is read from the COMMITTED PRE-CHANGE baseline, from the committed scenario definitions, or from the prior receipt itself -- the three sources the 2026-08-14 R-18 amendment names as facts of the question. It contains no post-change value, so no brief built from it can carry the answer.

pre_change_sources.why_each_cluster_names_its_own_capture: Each investigable cluster carries pre_change_capture, the sha its own how_the_defect_was_measured block already names in prose. Structured rather than only stated, for the reason the frontier gives for via: a route named only in a sentence is unverified prose beside a verified count, and a brief assembled from the wrong capture would pose the question against a side nobody disputed. scripts/investigator_brief.py reads this field and reads the baseline out of that git object, never off disk -- the working tree's copy is the post-change side, which is the answer.

Handed `cast_timeline[1]/resource_cost: 100.0 -> 0.0`, the investigator could not know that 100.0 is Force of Will's rank-5 mana cost and 0.0 is the second Dark Sphere charge's -- two different casts, one address. It computed W's cost from the cached ability rows, was right about it, and certified an old value nobody had disputed. clusters.defect_in_the_prior_brief: The correction did not change entries in place; it replaced four hand-written lists with derived ones of different length, different order and different membership, and rewrote the fifth from module prose into declaration prose. Every one of the seventeen leaves was then briefed as an isolated positional value pair. Three shapes result and none of them is a question about a mechanic. A member that SURVIVED with a new ordinal reads as a value change -- `setup[0]: "Q" -> "E"` on a list whose post-change membership still holds Q. A member that was REMOVED shifts every later ordinal -- `cast_order[2]: "E" -> "W"` on the 39-splinter scenario, where the retirement dropped the Q2 row that 39 splinters cannot buy. And a list that grew reads as absent-to-value at its new tail -- `consume[1]`, `sources[4]`, `aoe/passive`. An investigator handed any of these is asked to choose between two sentences about two different abilities as though one replaced the other, which is a question nobody asked, and it must still return a member of R-19's three-way set.

escalated_by_this_docket.what: Twenty of the twenty-two docketed dissents are ordinal or membership artifacts of positional pairing over lists that carry no IDENTITY_FIELD. `leaf_report` pairs by `event_id` where a member has one and falls back to positional pairing otherwise -- correctly, fail-closed, and documented as such. What nobody wrote down is the consequence: for `cast_timeline` (identified by `slot` + `ordinal`) and for the rotation record's bare-string lists (identified by their own value), an insertion or a removal re-addresses every later member, and every re-addressed member becomes a value diff that R-15 sends to an investigator.
escalated_by_this_docket.why_it_is_escalated_and_not_fixed_here: Widening identity pairing is a change to the instrument every committed allowlist and every oracle receipt in the campaign addresses leaves through -- each spells the baseline's ordinal, which is the address `leaf_report` promises to keep. Changing that at the campaign's close would re-address the very artifacts this docket is built from, and it is a semantic change to a gate, which R-30 and R-32 both bind. It belongs to whoever schedules the re-adjudications, ahead of them. (Superseded by `resolved` below, which is what it asked for: the widening lands ahead of the re-adjudications rather than never.)

escalated_by_this_docket.carried_by: this file, and the cluster rows above that measure it

resolved.what_landed: `leaf_report` now reaches both lists this entry names. A record whose identity is spelled apart -- an origin field beside that origin's own ordinal, which is what a `cast_timeline` row carries -- is paired by it exactly as an `event_id`-bearing record is; one concept, two spellings. A list of bare strings, whose members have no fields to be identified by at all, is paired by the strings themselves.
resolved.the_guard_that_keeps_it_a_correction: String pairing applies only when the two lists differ in length. An equal-length list gained and lost nothing, so positional pairing is already the honest reading there and a substitution stays the single `text_change` it is -- which matters because a membership transition can be adjudicated by citation under the 2026-08-14 R-15 amendment and a `text_change` never can. Numbers are excluded from value identity outright: R-15 grades a numeric move by `percent` and `abs_delta`, and re-spelling one as a removal plus an addition would throw both away. Record identity needs no such guard, because a record's identity is never its value.
resolved.what_it_does_not_decide: No dissent. Every cluster's remedy is unchanged and still a fresh investigator that has read neither the prior receipts nor this docket; clause 2 still re-opens the producing correction if the re-adjudication sustains. What is removed is the instrument defect that would have handed the next investigator the same mis-posed question -- which is why this entry said the widening belongs ahead of the re-adjudications.
resolved.gate: tests/test_golden_snapshot.py::TestOriginOrdinalIdentity and ::TestBareStringListIdentity. Both carry R-05 negatives that reproduce the defect on demand: stripping `ordinal` from the cast fixture restores the exact `cast_timeline[1]/resource_cost: 100.0 -> 0.0` brief the three C6 receipts answered, and the equal-length assertion fails if the guard is dropped.
resolved.measured_on_the_commit_that_lands_it: R-01 rows 2 and 3 both report the snapshot identical to their committed baselines, before and after -- the widening re-addresses nothing at the tip, because the tip has no diff to re-address. Expected qualifying occurrences: 0, from that enumerated population.
